short: Proc macros for the application layer
is: The application layer's proc-macro crate: `#[use_case]` (dependency injection into a use-case method, with `#[unit]`/`#[lazy_unit]` brackets) and `#[derive(WithPorts)]` (the ports-bag plumbing of a use-case namespace), consumed only by `application`.
conventions: One file per macro under `src/`, each exposing a `pub(crate) fn expand_*(…) -> syn::Result<TokenStream2>`; `lib.rs` holds only the `#[proc_macro_*]` entry points and turns an `Err` into `compile_error!`.
Emitted code names its targets as `crate::…` (`crate::ports::WithPorts`, `crate::Ports`, `crate::LazyUnit`, `crate::lazy_unit::…`), so both macros only expand correctly inside `application`.
Bad input is a spanned `syn::Error` on the offending token, never a panic; every error has a compile-fail case in `tests/ui/`.

`#[unit]` opens the unit before the body and may not be combined with `#[ports]` (a pool read would hold a second connection while the unit is open) or `#[lazy_unit]`; a use case that reads or calls out before writing takes `#[lazy_unit]` and calls `uow.open()` right before its first write.

Both unit forms scope the body in a task-local frame; opening a unit while an enclosing use case's unit is open debug-asserts (the nested-unit guard, which also catches a use case opening its own unit after a called one settled another).
A fn with a parameter typed `Query` or `*Query` may not carry `#[unit]` or `#[lazy_unit]`: a Query never writes.

fs.name: Cargo.toml
fs.role: proc-macro = true; deps proc-macro2 + quote + syn(full) + dev-dep trybuild, all from `[workspace.dependencies]`

fs.name: src/lib.rs
fs.role: the two entry points: `#[use_case]` attribute, `#[derive(WithPorts)]` with its `#[ports]` helper attribute

fs.name: src/use_case.rs
fs.role: splits an async `&self` method into a private `<name>_inner_injected` (the body, all params) and a same-named wrapper without the injected params; `#[unit]` begins before the body, `#[lazy_unit]` hands the body a `LazyUnit`, both commit on `Ok` and roll back on `Err`; a fn that injects nothing passes through unchanged

fs.name: src/with_ports.rs
fs.role: derives `WithPorts` from the single `#[ports]` field: a child (`&'a Parent<'a>`) delegates to its parent and the parent gains a snake_case accessor building the child; `#[ports(is_root = true)]` returns the field itself and emits no accessor

fs.name: tests/ui/
fs.role: one compile-fail case per macro error, each with its `.stderr`

refs.title: Transactions as a capability — a compile-enforced Unit of Work in the private store
refs.governs: src/use_case.rs: the generated wrapper is the begin/commit/rollback bracket of a use case

refs.title: The Application Layer — Use Cases, DTOs and Ports
refs.governs: src/use_case.rs + src/with_ports.rs: the shape of a use-case method and of the namespaces that carry the Ports bag

notes: The wrapper's own `begin`/`commit`/`rollback` calls carry `#[allow(clippy::disallowed_methods)]`; `application/clippy.toml` bans those three methods everywhere else in that crate.
A `#[use_case]` needs a `self` receiver and an `async fn`. One that injects nothing is passed through unchanged, so a plain method may carry the attribute too.
The inner fn is private and `#[doc(hidden)]`; the outer fn keeps the original visibility and attributes.
The derive's child form builds the struct from the parent field alone, so a child namespace cannot carry extra fields; a root can.
`.stderr` files are rustc output: regenerate with `TRYBUILD=overwrite cargo test -p application-macros` and check both the local toolchain and the floating stable CI uses.
